title: Violin Concerto in D major
hook: Written in a few weeks by a lake in Switzerland, rejected by the violinist it was meant for, loved ever since.

painting.title: Panoramic View of the Alps, Les Dents du Midi
painting.pairingNote: Painted on the shore of Lake Geneva the year before Tchaikovsky wrote the concerto at Clarens, at the same end of the lake; bright Alpine air for his sunniest concerto.

facts: Tchaikovsky wrote the concerto in 1878 in Clarens, on Lake Geneva in Switzerland, where he had gone to recover after the collapse of his marriage the year before. It was finished in about a month.

His pupil, the violinist Iosif Kotek, joined him there. They played through Lalo’s *Symphonie espagnole* together, which may have sparked the idea, and since Tchaikovsky was not a violinist, Kotek helped him shape the solo part. Tchaikovsky threw out his first slow movement and wrote the Canzonetta in its place; the discarded movement survives as a piece for violin and piano.

He dedicated the concerto to the violinist Leopold Auer, but Auer would not play it, and the planned premiere was cancelled. Adolph Brodsky gave the first performance in Vienna on 4 December 1881, with Hans Richter conducting, and the dedication went to him instead.
The critic Eduard Hanslick called the concerto long and pretentious, and the finale “odorously Russian”. Auer later played and taught it, in his own edited version.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a sweet tune that grows into fireworks (I), a sad song for muted violin (II), a whirling Russian dance (III).

movements.heading: Allegro moderato
movements.summary: It begins quietly, almost shyly, and the soloist enters with a few searching phrases before singing the main tune. The movement is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]], but what you notice is how the two lyrical themes are spun out into more and more brilliant decoration. Before the themes return, the violin plays a long [[cadenza|cadenza]] alone, ending on a [[trill|trill]].

mainIdeas.name: The introduction
mainIdeas.description: a gentle, hesitant phrase in the violins of the orchestra. As in the First Piano Concerto, this opening idea never returns.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a sweet, lilting, [[cantabile|cantabile]] tune for the solo violin, in D major.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a more tender, yearning melody, high on the solo violin.

stops.hear: The orchestra’s violins, quietly, play a gentle phrase; the music hesitates and waits
The solo violin enters alone with a few rising, searching phrases
stops.happening: The soloist’s entry, like a short cadenza

stops.hear: The violin sings a sweet, lilting tune over a light accompaniment
The tune is repeated and decorated; quick runs and leaps
stops.happening: Theme 1 spun out. The [[exposition|exposition]] grows more brilliant

stops.hear: Calmer and more tender: a yearning melody, high on the violin
The violin climbs, races and sparkles; the tension rises
The orchestra alone plays the main tune at full strength, grand and swaggering
stops.happening: The first [[tutti|tutti]]: the climax of the exposition

stops.hear: The music turns restless and wanders through new keys
The violin returns with a delicate variation of the main tune, then brilliant passage-work
stops.happening: The development, with the tune in C major

stops.hear: The orchestra bursts in once more with the main tune, heroic and loud, then stops
stops.happening: A second tutti, in F major, leading to the cadenza

stops.hear: The violin alone: chords, runs, some of its highest notes, sudden pauses; it ends on a long trill
While the violin is still trilling, a flute quietly plays the main tune
The yearning melody returns, now in D major

stops.label: Last two minutes
stops.hear: Faster; the violin races to the top, and the orchestra ends with a burst

notice: Listen for the moment the cadenza ends. The violin’s trill does not stop: it becomes the accompaniment for the flute, which brings back the main tune.
Compare the main tune at ≈ 1:10, soft and sweet, with the orchestra’s version at ≈ 7:05, loud and stately.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Hilary Hahn with Vasily Petrenko and the Royal Liverpool Philharmonic, recorded in Liverpool in November 2008. She plays the finale complete, without the traditional cuts. On the Spotify album the Tchaikovsky is tracks 4–6, after Jennifer Higdon’s concerto.

movements.heading: Canzonetta: Andante
movements.summary: A “little song” in G minor, sad and simple. A few soft woodwind chords open it, like a hymn. Then the violin, with a mute on its bridge, sings a long, lonely melody. A brighter middle section passes, the song returns, and soft chords in the orchestra lead without a pause into the finale.

mainIdeas.name: The woodwind opening
mainIdeas.description: a few slow, soft chords, like a hymn.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a sad, simple melody on the muted solo violin, sweet and melancholy at once.

stops.hear: The woodwinds alone play a few slow, soft chords
The violin, veiled and quiet, sings a sad, simple melody
stops.happening: The main song, in G minor. The soloist plays [[muted|muted]]

stops.hear: The mood brightens; the melody flows more freely
stops.happening: The middle section, in E-flat major

stops.hear: The sad melody returns, with woodwind lines weaving around it
The violin falls silent; soft, slowly changing chords in the orchestra

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: The chords grow, and the finale bursts straight in

notice: The mute makes the violin sound far away. In the finale it is taken off, and the difference is immediate.

movements.heading: Finale: Allegro vivacissimo
movements.summary: A Russian dance that keeps getting faster. After a loud start and a short, free passage for the violin, the soloist launches a quick, stamping tune, played low on its thickest string for a rough, earthy sound. A second, swaying tune is played over a drone in the bass, like a village band, and is varied several times. The dance wins in the end, at top speed.

mainIdeas.name: The dance
mainIdeas.description: a quick, stamping tune, first played on the violin’s lowest string, gritty and resonant.

mainIdeas.name: The village tune
mainIdeas.description: slower and swaying, over a drone, in A major.

stops.hear: A loud, lively burst from the orchestra
The violin alone, free and fiery, gathering speed
A quick, stamping dance on the violin, low and rough at first
stops.happening: The main theme, in D major

stops.hear: The orchestra takes up the dance, loud
A little slower: the violin plays a swaying tune over a steady drone in the bass
stops.happening: The second theme, *Poco meno mosso*, in A major

stops.hear: Slower still and sadder: woodwinds and violin trade a plaintive phrase
The violin speeds up, little by little, and the dance returns
stops.happening: *Poco a poco stringendo*. The main theme, now in F major

stops.hear: The swaying drone tune returns
stops.happening: The second theme again, in G major

stops.hear: The dance once more
stops.happening: The main theme, for the last time

stops.label: Last 90 seconds
stops.hear: Faster and faster, to a brilliant finish

notice: Listen to the bass during the second theme. The low strings hold one note, like the drone of a bagpipe or a village fiddler’s open string.
The tempo creeps up. The final pages are much faster than the opening dance.

notes.title: Cuts
notes.body: For decades many violinists, following Auer’s edition, made small cuts in this finale, so its length varies from recording to recording.

threads.title: Song and dance
threads.body: Every movement is either a song (the lyrical themes of I, the Canzonetta) or a dance (the finale and the orchestra’s grand version of the main tune).

threads.title: The violin in many voices
threads.body: Sweet in the first theme, veiled with a mute in the Canzonetta, rough and rustic in the finale.

threads.title: Russian colour
threads.body: What Hanslick complained of is now part of the attraction: the drone, the folk-like tunes, the rough low string and the accelerating dance of the finale.
